summary: Frontend-only testing of Igreja Casa da Oração torn-paper editorial landing. All requested flows verified across desktop (1920), tablet (768) and mobile (390). Zero console/page errors on load. All 10 named data-testid sections/regions exist (hero, about, services, events, ministries, sermon, gallery, location, footer, header). Header nav (nav-início, nav-sobre, nav-cultos, nav-ministérios, nav-eventos, nav-contato) and CTAs (hero-cta-primary → #sobre, hero-cta-secondary → #cultos, visit-us-btn → #contato) all scroll smoothly via Lenis and land with the target section's top ≈ 80px (matches -80 offset). Header becomes translucent (bg-paper/85 backdrop-blur-md) after scrolling past 40px. Contact form: empty submit shows Portuguese error toast ('Preencha o nome e o e-mail, por favor.'); filled submit shows success toast ('Mensagem recebida! Entraremos em contacto em breve.') and clears name/email/message inputs. map-iframe present; directions-link href points to google.com/maps. Mobile menu opens on mobile-menu-toggle click, closes when a mobile-nav link is tapped, and scrolls to correct section. Paper sheet leaves dark background (#171411 confirmed via body bg rgb(23,20,17)) visible on both sides at every breakpoint: desktop 320px each side, tablet 32px each side, mobile 12px each side. No horizontal overflow observed.
critical_code_review_comments: Header.jsx duplicates the anchor-scroll logic that is also inlined inside Hero.jsx CTAs; consider extracting a small useSmoothScroll hook to keep behavior consistent.
Location.jsx form only validates presence of name/email — no email format validation (e.g. missing '@'). Minor UX polish, not a blocker.
Contact form message field is not cleared vs. validated; success path clears it (already handled). No issue.
All interactive elements correctly expose data-testid attributes as required by the spec.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Frontend-only app, no backend. Lenis smooth scroll lands sections at top ≈ 80 due to -80 offset — assertions should allow that. Nav testids use lowercase original Portuguese labels including diacritics (e.g. nav-início, nav-ministérios). All flows currently passing.
